content: The document outlines detailed procedures and guidelines for poison information centers, focusing on their operations, data collection, and service delivery. 1. Expert Guidelines for Antidote Stocking in Emergency Hospitals Hospitals providing emergency care should adhere to expert consensus guidelines for stocking antidotes. These guidelines ensure that essential antidotes are readily available to manage poisoning cases effectively. 2. Snakebite Management Guidelines The second edition of the snakebite management guidelines provides comprehensive recommendations for treating snakebite victims. It includes protocols for antivenom administration, supportive care, and monitoring of complications. 3. Statistical Data on Enquiries Poison centers must collect detailed data on incoming and outgoing communications, including telephone calls, emails, and personal consultations. This data should categorize enquiries by type, location, agent involved, and time of occurrence. It is essential to document the demographics of callers and patients, including age, gender, and exposure circumstances. 4. Statistical Data on Incidents Centers should record the total number of poisoning incidents, distinguishing between those with and without exposed individuals. Data should include the circumstances of exposure, types of agents involved, and the severity of cases. Specific attention should be given to incidents involving pregnant patients or unusual toxicological scenarios. 5. Statistical Data on Cases Detailed records of cases should include patient demographics, exposure circumstances, and outcomes. Data should also cover cases by agent type, age group, and gender, with particular focus on severe outcomes such as fatalities. 6. Laboratory Investigations Poison centers should maintain operational analytical equipment and document the number and type of laboratory investigations conducted. These may include toxicological analyses, drug screenings, and environmental testing. Centers should ensure the availability of necessary supplies and reagents. 7. Facilities for Patient Management Poison centers should report on the availability of beds for poisoned patients, outpatient consultations, and access to specialized treatments such as hemodialysis or advanced diagnostic facilities like MRI. This ensures comprehensive care for poisoning cases. 8. Antidotes and Antivenoms Centers must maintain an updated list of available antidotes and antivenoms, documenting their usage and distribution. Any new formulations or developments should be noted to improve treatment protocols. 9. Preventive Activities Poison centers should engage in community prevention efforts, such as public education campaigns and toxicovigilance activities. This includes investigating toxic situations, issuing alerts, and reporting findings to authorities. 10. Advisory Roles Poison centers play a critical role in advising governmental and other bodies on safety measures, regulatory activities, and the registration of hazardous substances. 11. Training and Education Centers should organize training courses for healthcare professionals and participate in educational activities. This includes undergraduate and postgraduate curricular studies to enhance knowledge in toxicology and poison management. 12. Research Activities Poison centers should conduct clinical, analytical, and epidemiological research. These activities should be well-documented, including objectives, partners, funding sources, and outcomes. 13. Publications Centers should produce and disseminate publications, reports, and educational materials. Staff contributions to scientific literature, such as case reports and articles, should also be documented. 14. National and International Meetings Poison centers should actively participate in and organize national and international meetings, workshops, and cooperative projects. These activities foster collaboration and knowledge exchange among professionals. 15. Budget and Resource Allocation Centers should report their annual budgets, including staff and operating costs. Any changes from the previous year and allocations for new activities should be detailed. 16. Main Requirements of the Center Poison centers should outline their primary needs, including technical, financial, and collaborative support, to enhance their operations and interactions with other centers. 17. Standard Operating Procedures for Handling Poison Enquiries Poison centers should follow a structured approach to handle enquiries, including taking caller details, reviewing resources, and providing tailored responses. Calls should be logged accurately, and referrals to specialists should be made when necessary. 18. Assessment of Call Handling Centers should evaluate the performance of specialists in handling calls, ensuring that they provide accurate information, conduct risk assessments, and use appropriate language for the caller's understanding. 19. User Satisfaction Surveys Poison centers should collect feedback from users through satisfaction surveys. These surveys assess the promptness, helpfulness, and adequacy of the advice provided, ensuring continuous improvement in service delivery. This comprehensive framework ensures that poison centers operate efficiently, provide high-quality care, and contribute to public health and safety.
